searchText: What's the reason? Afraid of being hacked? that much ETH would definitely be an attractive honeypot Payment channnels are the proper solution here. Every mining pool should be using them. who is going to educate 300k miners? ux of that? which exchange supports it? explorer?…. Presumably the pool. 😆 I think the disagreement here is likely that you think people should be able to hash on Ethereum without being capable of using Ethereum for simple transactions. And I can understand *why* one would feel that way, but I don't feel particularly bad that people are paying ridiculous fees because they can't be bothered to learn how to use the thing they are trying to mine. new miners join every day who don’t even know what gas is Definitely, same for dapp users. We should all be working toward educating those people on how to actually use Ethereum rather than just giving them solutions that hurt their security and their income. education is not necessary if ui/ux of these tools were good IMO, we should all be strongly encouraging users to *not* send directly to exchanges and educate them on how to use an actual wallet (e.g., MetaMask or whatever). Using a blockchain is fundamentally different from using traditional software. You have to learn at least a little bit (like how to install MetaMask and secure your recovery words). if small miners mine to a private wallet, they’ll need to send the transaction to the exchange themselves = expensive They can do it on their own schedule, rather than on the pool's schedule. And the costs don't get socialized across the pool like Ethermine does (which I'm amazing its power users put up with). bills need to be paid (in usd)? that’s why we added polygon 😖 Really? Polygon? Of all of the layer 2 options you had to choose the *worst* of them. 😖 all of the existing l2 solutions were not made for large usage we looked into all popular ones Why not zkSync? While they are still centralized, at least their system design is good and they can become decentralized. either crappy Ui/Ux, no dex liquidity, no explorer (actually, I may be thinking of poly-something else, looks like Polygon is Matic rebranded, and while I'm not a fan of Matic it isn't the *worst*) no dex Why do you need a DEX? allows small miners to settle their gains every day in usd tokens. The idea with payment channels is just to make it so the user has ownership of the tokens ASAP (can do payouts every second or minute if you want) without incurring any costs. The user can then settle the payment channel at their leisure and use whatever tools they want from there. This way Ethermine doesn't have to have custody of hasher funds for any longer than a very brief period of time, and you can push the operating cost of withdraws onto the hashers. It gets even easier with mixed-custody system (limited trust, but not trustless). and who’s going to constantly educate them? do we both remember the 1559 miner channel? now that times 30000 Your points work well in theory but not in practice I think the fundamental difference here is that you want to make money, while I want to spread the Good Word. I am more interested in gaining users who actually *use* Ethereum, rather than just people who trade ETH on some centralized exchange. polygon supports that vision It is better than nothing, I agree. I still don't think it is the right solution for miner payouts, and I somewhat disagree that Polygon pushes Ethereum's vision forward since it isn't a trustless/censorship resistant platform (at least last I checked). can add more ripe solutions with time let’s see how this goes ethermine is the first pool Hey everyone, Was reading about UUPS (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822), and was curious about what this piece of code is trying to prevent specifically? ``` contract LibraryLock is LibraryLockDataLayout { // Ensures no one can manipulate the Logic Contract once it is deployed. // PARITY WALLET HACK PREVENTION modifier delegatedOnly() { require(initialized == true, "The library is locked. No direct 'call' is allowed"); _; } function initialize() internal { initialized = true; } } ``` an old mishap from 2017 https://medium.com/cybermiles/i-accidentally-killed-it-and-evaporated-300-million-6b975dc1f76b i think. though there was another Parity wallet hack before that, maybe that's what i refers to I understand the need to restrict anyone from calling `selfdestruct`, but I'm not following whe purpose of `delegatedOnly` and why it's been assigned to the `transfer` function
